analysis.title: Top Stories (Mitch Jeter, GS Sales/Trading), 13 Nov 2026
key_insights: US October PPI prints at 8:30am ET. GS projects final demand +0.3% m/m vs consensus +0.4% (prior +1.3%), ex-food and energy +0.2% vs consensus +0.3% (prior +0.7%), and ex-food, energy and trade +0.3% vs consensus +0.3% (prior +0.5%). GS is below consensus on the headline and core.
The IEA says global oil markets will swing to a surplus for the first time since the start of the Iran conflict as Persian Gulf exports recover. It raised its 2026 supply estimate by 920,000 b/d.
A shortage of available oil supertankers is constraining US crude exports. Shippers are hiring smaller vessels and directing more cargoes to Europe, per the head of the Port of Corpus Christi.
Japan's Satsuki Katayama said officials will work closely with Washington to act against rapid one-sided yen moves, after the yen briefly weakened past 160 per dollar.
China's October credit growth missed forecasts, with new loans contracting on weak borrowing demand. China's M2 grew +7.1% y/y in October vs consensus +7.2%.
Bloomberg documents show a Chinese company founded by Alice Huang obtained restricted Nvidia chips. The report says this sets up a US-China showdown over AI chip controls.

Nvidia received multiple downgrades: Truist cut to Hold (PT $174) and Craig-Hallum cut to Hold (PT $180). Applied Materials was cut to Hold at Summit Insights and Broadcom to Neutral at Redburn (PT $398.46). The semiconductor ratings skew negative in the day's list.

WSJ reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang surrendered late Wednesday after weeks of denying infidelity allegations and fighting to remain in his job. The note's account is a single WSJ-sourced report of the CEO's exit.
Meta's personal AI assistants (Muse, Instinct and others) can now make purchases on behalf of cardholders, per WSJ. The WSJ describes the move as generating buzz about AI agents reshaping payments.

Microsoft's global outage entered a second day, with Outlook, Teams and Copilot disruptions hitting governments and businesses in over 70 countries. The company said it was seeing signs of server stability.
GS momentum baskets: Momentum (GSPRHIMO) had its best outperformance day in GS records vs the 3m Mo (GSPRHMO3) and 6m Mo (GSPRHMO6) baskets.

Fed speaker calendar is heavy: Goolsbee (CNBC, 8:30am), Collins (9:10am opening remarks, 10:35am Bloomberg TV), Logan (9:40am), Bowman (10:50am), Daly (12:00pm) and Jefferson (7:00pm) on technology and productivity.
